chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from one of his companions, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'We have hired workers, so we make them cultivate. They come to us and say: We have estimated this crop to be such and such. So give it to us, and we guarantee for you that we will give you your share based on this estimate.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it has matured?' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with this.' I said: 'Then after that he comes to us and says: The estimate did not turn out as I estimated, and it has decreased.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So when it increases, does he return [the excess] to you?' I said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So you may take it with the complete estimate. Just as when it increases it is for him, similarly when it decreases it is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on agricultural sharecropping contracts based on estimated yield?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility of 'hazr' (estimation) in sharecropping, a practice where the tenant guarantees a specific yield based on an initial assessment. Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the risk of variance—whether the crop exceeds or falls short of the estimate—remains with the worker, ensuring fairness and preventing dispute over the final distribution. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for validating commercial flexibility in agriculture while maintaining contractual integrity.
